title: Mix Up Your Practice
coreMove: Design practice so the learner has to discriminate among similar cases and choose the right move before using it.
sourcePressure: The chapter attacks blocked repetition: one skill repeated in a row can look strong during practice while leaving the learner weak at selection, discrimination, and transfer.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must avoid praising variety for its own sake; the point is structured mixing that forces comparison and choice.

sourceAnchors.name: Vince Dooley
sourceAnchors.detail: University of Georgia football coach from 1964 to 1988, with 201 wins, six conference titles, and a national championship, described interleaved weekly practice for fundamentals, small-group maneuvers, special plays, and mental rehearsal.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Vince Dooley did not make Saturday readiness from one drill repeated straight through; the week mixed fundamentals, plays, adjustments, and mental walk-throughs.

sourceAnchors.name: Kerr and Booth beanbag study
sourceAnchors.detail: Children who practiced tossing beanbags at two-foot and four-foot buckets outperformed those who practiced only at the three-foot target when later tested at three feet.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The children who never practiced the exact three-foot toss learned the range well enough to own the target in between.

sourceAnchors.name: Sebastian Leitner
sourceAnchors.detail: Developer of the Leitner box system, a spaced flashcard method that moves missed cards back to more frequent practice.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A Leitner box is a small physical refusal to let every card receive the same treatment forever.

hook: Do not open by saying learning is harder than it looks
Do not use a generic desk-and-notes image
Do not start with a broad claim about students today
counterintuition: Do not use the shell easier is not better
Do not flatten the chapter into struggle is good
Do not contrast comfort and growth in generic coaching language
tryThisNow: Do not write set a timer and reflect
Do not ask for a vague study audit
Do not use a reusable close-your-notes prompt without a chapter-specific action
examples: No repeated mug, marker, dosing cup, bike helmet, radiator, bus depot, classroom, or narrow-kitchen shells
No six examples that all start with a timestamp and a named protagonist
No generic student rereads notes scene unless the visible beat changes the method

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective reveal, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Daniel, a civil-engineering student sorting beam-load problems
exampleSpecs.audience: students who complete problem sets by type and cannot identify the type later
exampleSpecs.stakes: the final gives no heading that says which formula belongs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he shuffles shear, bending, and deflection problems, names the type first, then solves only after choosing the method
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Three unlabelled diagrams sit under a desk lamp.
mustAvoid: another all-math drill without visible discrimination

exampleSpecs.domain: Sophie, a pastry apprentice learning laminated dough faults
exampleSpecs.audience: craft learners who repeat one correction until it feels easy
exampleSpecs.stakes: service depends on identifying butter leakage, underproofing, and overhandling by sight
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she lines up three failed croissants, names the fault before touching the dough, and changes the next fold based on the diagnosis
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Butter beads shine on one croissant seam.

exampleSpecs.domain: Marco, a tennis coach rebuilding serve return practice
exampleSpecs.audience: athletes who look sharp against one predictable feed
exampleSpecs.stakes: match play requires reading slice, kick, and flat serves without warning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he stops the basket of identical feeds and calls random serve types so the player must read toss and shoulder before moving
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 5:32 p.m., Marco drags the ball basket away from the baseline.

exampleSpecs.domain: Ingrid, a pathology resident comparing look-alike slides
exampleSpecs.audience: medical trainees who memorize classic images but miss neighbors
exampleSpecs.stakes: the exam and the lab both require separating similar patterns
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: her attending asks what it is not, forcing Ingrid to contrast two near-neighbor diagnoses before naming the slide
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Tell me the mimic first," the attending says.

exampleSpecs.domain: Tomás, a jazz guitarist practicing chord substitutions
exampleSpecs.audience: musicians who drill one progression until it collapses in performance
exampleSpecs.stakes: the band modulates unexpectedly during rehearsal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show his change from twenty identical ii-V-I runs to a shuffled chart stack that makes him choose the substitution by ear
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Tomás a month to hear the wrong practice.

exampleSpecs.domain: Adaeze, a customs officer trainee identifying counterfeit documents
exampleSpecs.audience: security trainees who need flexible discrimination under pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: a false pass or false stop can harm real travelers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she rotates passports, visas, and work permits from different countries and must state the feature that made each suspicious before checking the guide
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which document is wrong if every seal looks almost right?

skillTargets: spot when blocked practice is flattering immediate performance
design mixed practice around near-neighbor discrimination
protect enough structure so interleaving does not become chaos

tryThisNowSpec: Take three problem types you usually practice separately, shuffle one example of each, and write the label before solving any of them.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
